cards.text: A pigeon lands directly on your bag, considers you with the flat, ancient judgement pigeons reserve for people who look like they're up to something, and doesn't move.
You've heard the stories — fate-types collect near omens the way flies collect near anything else. You have no idea if this counts. The pigeon, notably, does not clarify.
It flies off eventually, satisfied or bored, impossible to say which. You feel, absurdly, like your next piece of luck has already been decided somewhere above you.
